_comment: Codex Compatibility Registry data, format 1. Validated by src/codex_auto_resume/compat.py
and by tests/test_compat.py before it can ship or be served.
This file is the bundled baseline of a release, and the same path on the main branch is
what a refresh fetches - only when a person asks, from the Diagnostics page or an update
check. Remote data may only restrict: an entry here can mark a capability INCOMPATIBLE for
an exact version or a range, and can mark one VERIFIED only for an exact version whose
local checks already pass. A failed local check always wins.
The evidence rule: a VERIFIED entry has to cite an evidence file whose recorded
codex_version is that exact version and whose verdict is PASS, and a VERIFIED engine
lists engine_present and exact_thread_recovery both. The files under docs/evidence/compat
are written from one machine's own records of that version - the product's engine
reports and the recoveries it made - as counts and times, never conversation content.
A capability is VERIFIED only where a real recovery on that version exercised it and
none failed. CHECKED records that the local checks passed on that version and nothing
confirmed it further: v0.6.7 shows it, and v0.6.5 and v0.6.6 skip it - their validator
passes over a state it does not know - so it moves nothing they decide. A capability with
neither resolves through the local checks - COMPATIBLE where they pass - which is what the
product did before the registry existed. A local check that fails on a version the data
checked or verified reads as FAILED_HERE in v0.6.7: this machine, not the Codex version.
`sequence` only ever goes up. A refresh refuses a document with a lower sequence than the
one it would replace, and a cached document older than the bundled baseline is set aside.
`expires_at` is about 90 days after `published_at`: past it, a fetched copy's VERIFIED
and CHECKED entries stop counting while its INCOMPATIBLE ones never expire, so data carrying them
is republished before then. The bundled copy never
expires. `min_product` is the oldest product that reads format 1: v0.6.5, the first release
that carries the registry.
`signature`, `key_id` and `requires_signature` are reserved: a document that requires a
signature is refused whole until something verifies one.
